newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Mali said planning to buy Indonesian helicopters.
newsitem.headline: Mali said planning to buy Indonesian helicopters.

text.p: The West African nation of Mali plans to buy helicopters made by Indonesia's state-owned PT Industri Pesawat Terbang Nusantara, State Secretary Murdiono said on Friday.
Speaking to reporters after talks between President Suharto and Malian President Alpha Oumar Konare, Murdiono said Jakarta would in turn buy cotton from Mali.
"Mali has expressed a strong desire to buy helicopters from Indonesia. Indonesia suggested Mali ask for credit from the Islamic Development Bank (IDB) for the purchase," he said.
"Indonesia has offered to buy cotton and possibly wheat from Mali to ease the burden of repayment of the credit," he said.
Murdiono did not give details on how many helicopters and how much cotton or wheat would be involved.
Konare arrived on Thursday for a three day visit to Indonesia. He departs on Saturday.
